title: test(scripts): anchor the pnpm ledger entries on the root packageManager field
body:
Fixes #6447

The version-claim ledger's two `pnpm 10.x` entries now rest on a run instead of a sentence.

## The defect

`scripts/__tests__/doc-version-claims.test.ts` classified both entries `anchored`, and for an `anchored` entry carrying no machine-checked field the `why` string IS the anchor — a reviewer re-runs the command it describes. Theirs described a count:

> Anchored on the root packageManager field, pnpm@10.31.0: **17 corepack enable steps across 12 workflow files** mean the pnpm that installs and builds these packages in CI is the one that field names.

Measured on `d3bf4fa6f` in this worktree: **20 steps across 14 files**. Control, same sweep: **30** `node-version` declarations across **25** files — non-zero, so the grep root and the workflow directory are both real.

The half of the anchor that is a **field** (`pnpm@10.31.0`) was and is exactly right. The half that is a **count** had been wrong since four days after it was typed, and nothing in this repository was in a position to notice. Second site of the shape #6400 moved out of the `Node 22.x` entries; the card records why it needed a second derivation rather than one more field on that one.

## What this adds

**`manifestVersionField`** on `KnownClaim` — the third way an entry names its anchor and has the comparison RUN rather than re-verified, after `skeletonDep` and #6400's `workflowVersionKey`. It names a field of the root `package.json` whose value is the anchor.

A second **source** field rather than one more spelling on `workflowVersionKey`, because the two read different kinds of thing: that one sweeps a directory for every declaration of a GitHub-Actions key and reduces them to one major; this one reads a single field holding a tool and a version welded with an at-sign. Making one field mean both would put a "which kind of source is this" branch inside a derivation whose whole value is that it has none.

**Both halves of the value are judged.** A version-only comparison stays green if this workspace switches package managers and keeps a major — a page teaching `pnpm 10.x` against a field naming something else, with the gate reporting agreement. That is the vacuous anchor this file exists to notice, and it would have been shipped BY a card about vacuous anchors. So the tool the field names is compared against the toolchain word the claim leads with, read with the same `TOOLCHAIN` alternation the scan matched that word with in the first place — no new vocabulary enters the file for it.

Both `why` strings lose their `corepack enable` count. The count was never the anchor; it was the ARGUMENT for why the field is the anchor, and that argument does not need a live number to stand.

## The frozen counts in the docblock, and the policy applied

A card about a frozen count in a reason string cannot leave frozen counts in the prose arguing for the reason strings. **Policy, stated once in the file so the next reader can apply it:** a count describing the CURRENT tree is REMOVED and replaced by the run that re-takes it; a count recording what a change MEASURED when it landed is kept and ATTRIBUTED to that change, so it reads as history rather than as a reading of today.

| site (re-derived, pre-change line) | what it stated | tree on `d3bf4fa6f` | disposition |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `:368` "all 28 reading 22", "28 across 23" | 28 / 23 | **30 / 25** | removed — the `workflowVersionKey` assertion re-takes it every run; the qualitative claim (no declaration reads 20, every one reads 22) stays and is what the run checks |
| `:368` control "19 `corepack enable`" | 19 | **20** | removed with it |
| `:409` "28 across 23 … 27 rather than all 28 spelled `'22.x'`" | 28 / 23 / 27 | **30 / 25 / 29** | **attributed** — it is #6400's finding, so it is now stated AS OF that cut instead of as a reading of today |

The `:409` row is the one addition to the surface the card enumerated; it was declared in the dev claim comment before any code was written, not discovered in review. It qualifies under the bounded in-place rule: same file, same defect class, mechanical repair whose correct form is pinned by the file's own doctrine ("correcting 14 to 28 … reinstalls the same mechanism with a newer number"), no other claim holds this file, and no new verification surface.

## Verification

**Ablation, on the real tree, three red directions — this is the load-bearing evidence.** Each leg proved the mutation on disk by grepping for the injected AND the removed text (an editor's exit code proves nothing), and each restore was proved by **blob-hash equality against the HEAD blob plus an empty `git diff HEAD`**, never by an exit code. The script carried a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` restore anchored on an absolute `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` path.

HEAD blob of `package.json`: `08f4874ce8e042faced1a4bb9006a0231b6443fe`

| leg | mutation (injected hits / removed hits) | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 0 — baseline | none | **29 passed** |
| 1 — major `10.31.0` → `11.0.0` | 1 / 0 | **RED**, 1 failed / 28 passed |
| restore | — | blob `08f4874c…` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty |
| 2 — tool `pnpm` → `yarn`, major KEPT | 1 / 0 | **RED**, 1 failed / 28 passed |
| 3 — field deleted entirely | 1 / 0 | **RED**, 1 failed / 28 passed |
| final restore | — | blob `08f4874c…` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty |
| 4 — green again | none | **29 passed** |

Leg 1 produced, on both pages:

```
content/docs/guide/building-crud-app.md:12  the page states "pnpm 10.x" (major 10);
  the root package.json declares packageManager: "pnpm@11.0.0" (major 11)
```

Leg 2 is the one that matters for the design — the majors line up on purpose, so only the tool check can catch it:

```
content/docs/guide/quick-start.md:12  the page states "pnpm 10.x", a claim about pnpm;
  the root package.json declares packageManager: "yarn@10.31.0" - the page is teaching
  a tool this workspace is not built with, and the majors agreeing would not make that true
```

Leg 3:

```
content/docs/guide/building-crud-app.md :: manifestVersionField names packageManager,
  which the root package.json does not declare - there is no anchor to read
```

Both directions are also pinned **permanently** by a manifest fixture in the suite, not demonstrated once, for the reason #6400's workflow-directory fixture exists: a green anchor assertion looks exactly like an assertion that compared nothing.

**Test surface, re-derived rather than inherited.** All 3 test files in the repository that read `packageManager` — the field this change newly reads — live in `scripts/__tests__` (`git grep -l packageManager` over `*.test.ts` / `*.test.tsx` / `*.spec.ts`: 3 hits, **0** of them outside that directory; control, same sweep: 58 test files read `'package.json'`). That whole directory was run.

Every run below, and every ablation leg above, was re-run on the final commit `e85231bd4` after a wrap-only follow-up landed — a green union measured on a tree that is no longer head is not a reading about head. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01GgDDqh6YnkXqsnVTCa7wHk

| command | result |
|:--|:--|
| `vitest run scripts/__tests__/doc-version-claims.test.ts` | 29 passed (29) |
| `vitest run scripts/__tests__` | **91 files, 2586 tests, all passed** |
| the same three ablation legs, re-run on `e85231bd4` | RED / RED / RED, restores hash-proved again |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json` | 0 diagnostics |
| `pnpm lint:root` (`eslint .` as the repo spells it) | exit 0 — 0 errors, 29 pre-existing warnings |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | OK, 5834 tracked text files |
| `pnpm check:vi-mock-inherit` / `check:vi-mock-specifiers` | OK |
| `pnpm check:shell-escape-residue` | OK |
| `pnpm lint:coverage` | 46/46 packages, 0 outstanding |
| `pnpm type-check:coverage` | 45/46 via `type-check`, 0 errors outstanding |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — "2 file(s) changed … 1 changeset(s) added" |

**Typecheck coverage proved, not assumed.** `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json --listFiles` puts `scripts/__tests__/doc-version-claims.test.ts` in the program (1 hit, file 524 of 726). Controls both ways: `check-changeset-presence.test.ts` present (1 hit, must be), `apps/console/src/main.tsx` absent (0 hits, must be).

**Lint population and invariance, since `check-lint-coverage` is a debt ledger that does not execute eslint.** The population was read from eslint's own config resolution via `--format json`, not guessed: **222 files**, the full root-lint population, un-narrowed. The edited file is in it with **0 errors, 0 warnings**. `eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService` anywhere, so type-aware linting is off and a file's verdict is a function of its own text plus the flat config — neither of which this diff moves for any untouched file. (An extra run with `--no-inline-config` surfaces 1 error in `e2e/live/global-setup.ts:47`, a pre-existing `no-console` suppression this diff does not touch and not the spelling this repo's gate uses.)

**Control-byte discipline.** `grep -naP` for the raw control-byte class over both changed files: **0** hits; control, same expression machinery on the same file: 3082 hits.

## Changeset

Test-only, so the changeset declares no package — an empty frontmatter, which `check-changeset-presence` confirms is the accepted shape here (it reports no changeset was owed at all and one was added anyway).

## Boundaries

- `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` was **not** touched, and needed no edit: this card's surface is the ledger. #6448 owns a prose line on that page and is running in parallel.
- #6400's and #6409's landed `KNOWN_CLAIMS` entries were not edited. One of them carries a stale count of its own — the `ci-cd-pipeline.md :: Node 22.x` entry says "28 mentions of `ci.yml`" where `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` now holds **29**. Left alone on purpose and reported separately rather than folded in; that boundary is not addressed by this PR.
- Governed surfaces (`.claude/`, `docs/adr/`, `skills/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) and `content/docs/releases/` were not touched.
